title: What If Every Suitable Rooftop on Earth Had Solar Panels?

scenes.text: What if every suitable rooftop on Earth had solar panels? The answer is bigger than most people guess.
A Nature Climate Change study estimated they could generate up to 19,500 terawatt-hours of electricity a year.
With load shifting and batteries, that could cover about 65 percent of today's global electricity use.
That is roughly two-thirds of the world's power, from surfaces that already exist.
The authors estimate the shift could cool the planet by up to 0.13 degrees Celsius before 2050.
The catch: it needs batteries, shifting when we use power, and every suitable roof. Possible, not automatic.
